plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: Cascading chains of fragrant, pea-like flowers hang from twisting woody vines. They drape pergolas, walls and old trees in a haze of lilac-purple, and the scent drifts on warm spring air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (typically April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China; widely grown in gardens across temperate Asia, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine in a set direction. Chinese wisteria climbs counterclockwise, while Japanese wisteria climbs clockwise. Vines can live for well over a century.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms stand upright on sturdy stems and come in a wide range of colors and petal shapes. Tulip fields in full bloom look like stripes of bright color laid across the countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (peaking in April and into early May in the Netherlands)
plants.location: Netherlands, especially the bulb-growing region near Lisse, and temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: In 17th-century Holland, tulip bulbs became so valuable that some sold for more than the price of a canal house during the 'tulip mania' boom.

plants.name: Quercus robur
plants.description: The oak's spring flowers are easy to overlook. Slender, pale-green catkins dangle among the unfurling leaves, and tiny female flowers sit on the twigs. Together they signal the start of the oak's annual cycle.
plants.location: Woodlands, hedgerows and parkland across Europe, including the British Isles
plants.funFact: Oaks are wind-pollinated. A single mature tree can release millions of pollen grains, and only a few will reach a female flower.
